title: Can One Man Heal and Forgive?
thread: Isaiah 6:10 (God speaking) ends 'and be healed'; when Jesus gives the same warning in Mark 4:12 it ends 'and their sins should be forgiven them' (lest they be converted: forgiveness is what outsiders miss); Matthew 13:15 has 'and I should heal them' and says their eyes they have closed; the Bible does not say why the wording differs; in Mark 2:1-12 a man who could not walk is brought, Jesus first says 'Son, thy sins be forgiven thee' (2:5), some think only God can forgive sins (2:6-7), and Jesus heals him that they may know the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins (2:10); Luke 4:18 'he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted' backs the closing line about healing the heart
anchor_kjv: Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed. That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them. For this people’s heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them. When Jesus saw their faith, he said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, thy sins be forgiven thee. But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (he saith to the sick of the palsy,) The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised,
anchor_kjv_note: Every KJV verse quoted in the copy (Isaiah 6:10; Mark 4:12; Matthew 13:15; Mark 2:5, 2:10; Luke 4:18), joined, from data/kjv_full; the UK-G2 gate checks quotes against this text. anchor_ref stays Mark 2:1-12 (primary).
